Richard Stengel visits the Sawab Center in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, the first-ever multinational online messaging and engagement program in support of the global coalition against Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL)

On September 12, 2013, Stengel announced he would be leaving _TIME_ magazine for a role as Under Secretary of State for Public Diplomacy and Public Affairs,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-Pompeo-4) the role responsible for leading "America's public diplomacy outreach, which includes communications with international audiences, cultural programming, academic grants, educational exchanges, international visitor programs, and U.S. Government efforts to confront ideological support for terrorism," according to the State Department's website.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-41)

### Government service

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Richard_Stengel&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Government service")]

Stengel served as [President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States")[Obama's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Barack_Obama "Presidency of Barack Obama")[Under Secretary of State for Public Diplomacy and Public Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Under_Secretary_of_State_for_Public_Diplomacy_and_Public_Affairs "Under Secretary of State for Public Diplomacy and Public Affairs") from 2014 to 2016.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-Pompeo-4) Stengel modernized the State Department's communications efforts, including getting all embassies on social media and using new digital platforms to help America tell its story abroad.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-npr.org-42) Stengel led the department's counter-disinformation efforts, which included managing State's counter-ISIS messaging center, The Center for Strategic Counter Terrorism Communications, and started the first counter Russian disinformation hub at the department.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-npr.org-42) That ultimately led to an executive order creating the [Global Engagement Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Engagement_Center "Global Engagement Center"), tasked with countering disinformation globally.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-43) He also helped create a joint effort between the Peace Corps and the State Department called “English for All,” a whole-of-government effort to teach English around the world. In December 2016, Stengel became the longest serving Under Secretary of State for Public Diplomacy in American history.

In November 2020, Stengel was named a member of the [Joe Biden presidential transition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden_presidential_transition "Joe Biden presidential transition") Agency Review Team to support transition efforts related to the [U.S. Agency for Global Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Agency_for_Global_Media "U.S. Agency for Global Media").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-44)

### Other

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Richard_Stengel&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Other")]

See also: [Newsguard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newsguard "Newsguard")

Stengel was a strategic adviser at [Snap, Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snap,_Inc. "Snap, Inc.") from 2017 to 2021, working primarily on communications.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-45)

Stengel is currently an on-air analyst for MSNBC and NBC who comments on political news of the day.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-46) Stengel is also a member of the board of directors of CARE, the global humanitarian and poverty relief organization.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-47)

## National Service Movement

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Richard_Stengel&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: National Service Movement")]

In September 2007, Stengel wrote a _Time_ cover story called "The Case For National Service" in which he argued that Americans needed to redouble their efforts to get involved in community service and volunteerism, and that the presidential candidates needed to make the issue a top priority in the 2008 presidential campaign.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-Stengel2-48) Through this essay, he became involved with national service groups Be the Change, City Year, Civic Enterprises, and others to form [ServiceNation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ServiceNation "ServiceNation"), a coalition of more than 100 organizations dedicated to promoting national service and volunteerism.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-49)

ServiceNation announced that it had secured both U.S. presidential candidates to participate in Presidential Forum on National Service at Columbia University on September 11, 2008.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-50) Stengel served as co-moderator of the forum, along with PBS journalist [Judy Woodruff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judy_Woodruff "Judy Woodruff"), and both Senators [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") and [John McCain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCain "John McCain") answered questions in front of a live audience at [Columbia University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_University "Columbia University") about their plans for national service.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-51)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-52)

On September 12, 2008, Stengel was a featured speaker at the ServiceNation Summit in New York, along with [Caroline Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caroline_Kennedy "Caroline Kennedy"), Senator [Hillary Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton "Hillary Clinton"), First Lady [Laura Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Bush "Laura Bush") and New York City Mayor [Michael Bloomberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bloomberg "Michael Bloomberg").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-53) In February 2009, he testified alongside [Usher Raymond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Usher_Raymond "Usher Raymond"), former U.S. Senator [Harris Wofford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harris_Wofford "Harris Wofford") and others, in front of the [United States House Committee on Education and Labor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Committee_on_Education_and_Labor "United States House Committee on Education and Labor") about the importance of national service,[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-54) leading to the passage of the [Edward M. Kennedy Serve America Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_M._Kennedy_Serve_America_Act "Edward M. Kennedy Serve America Act") (H.R. 1388). Among other provisions, the bill helped to establish a Summer of Service Program, increase the number of [AmeriCorps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AmeriCorps "AmeriCorps") opportunities and establish a nationwide Call to Service Campaign.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-55)

Stengel was awarded Citizen of the Year at the Annual [National Conference on Citizenship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Conference_on_Citizenship "National Conference on Citizenship") on September 17, 2010.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-56) He has also been presented with the 2010 Lifetime of Idealism Award, awarded to him by City Year Washington, D.C. for "his commitment to promoting and expanding opportunities for Americans to serve".[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-CityYear-57)

## Published works

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Richard_Stengel&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Published works")]

Stengel has authored several books. His first was _January Sun: One Day, Three Lives, A South African Town_, a non-fiction work about the lives of three men in rural South Africa, published in 1990.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-Welsh-6)

Stengel is best known for is his collaboration with Nelson Mandela on Mandela's [autobiography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autobiography "Autobiography"), _[Long Walk to Freedom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long\_Walk\_to\_Freedom "Long Walk to Freedom")_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-Beresford-7) In 1992, he signed a ghostwriting deal with publishers [Little, Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little,_Brown "Little, Brown") to work on the book, having first been cleared by the [African National Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_National_Congress "African National Congress") as a suitable author.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-Beresford-7) The book was published in 1995, and was praised by the _[Financial Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial\_Times "Financial Times")_, which stated: "Their collaboration produced surely one of the great autobiographies of the 20th century".[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-58) Stengel later served as [co-producer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_producer "Film producer") of the 1996 [documentary film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Documentary_film "Documentary film")_[Mandela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandela\_(1996\_film) "Mandela (1996 film)")_, which was nominated for an [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-Time_Warner-12)

In 2000, Stengel published _You're Too Kind: A Brief History of Flattery,_ a popular history of [flattery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flattery "Flattery").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-Yardley-59)

_Mandela's Way: Fifteen Lessons on Life, Love and Courage_ was released in March 2010 and is based on Stengel's personal interactions with Nelson Mandela.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-60)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-Wilkie-61) The book drew praise from former U.S. President [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton"), as well as [Deepak Chopra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepak_Chopra "Deepak Chopra") and [Henry Louis Gates Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Louis_Gates_Jr. "Henry Louis Gates Jr.")[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-Wilkie-61)

In 2012, Stengel edited and wrote the lead essay for the book _The Constitution: The Essential User's Guide_, which explored the relevance of the [U.S. Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution "Constitution") in modern-day events.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-Aboul-Enein-62)

In 2019, Stengel published _Information Wars,_ which has been praised by Madeleine Albright, Walter Isaacson and Jon Meacham. It tells the story of his efforts to combat both Russian disinformation and ISIS messaging from the State Department, and the eventual formation of the [Global Engagement Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Engagement_Center "Global Engagement Center"), tasked with fighting the global epidemic of disinformation.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-Information_Wars-63) The book's final chapter details what can be done about disinformation.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-Information_Wars-63)

In December 2022, [Audible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audible_(service) "Audible (service)") released Stengel's 10-part podcast, _Mandela: The Lost Tapes_, which uses more than 60 hours of taped interviews Stengel did with Mandela for _Long Walk to Freedom_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-:0-9) The tapes had never before been released in their entirety.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-64) The podcast tells the story of Mandela's life, the making of _Long Walk to Freedom,_ and the unusual friendship between Mandela and Stengel.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-:0-9) The podcast was covered by [The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times"), [Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Post "Washington Post"), the [Today Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Today_(American_TV_program) "Today (American TV program)"), [The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian"), and [The Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Times "The Times") of London.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-:0-9)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-65)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-66)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-67)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-68)[AudioFile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AudioFile_(magazine) "AudioFile (magazine)") called it “a compelling work that makes history come alive.”[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-69)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Richard_Stengel&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Stengel is married to Mary Pfaff, a native of South Africa. They have two sons, Gabriel and Anton.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-Time_Warner-12) The couple met while Stengel was in South Africa working on [Nelson Mandela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Mandela "Nelson Mandela")'s autobiography. Mandela was godfather to their oldest son, Gabriel.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-Vargas-70)

## Honorary degrees

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Richard_Stengel&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Honorary degrees")]

Stengel delivered the commencement address for and received [honorary doctorates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honorary_doctorates "Honorary doctorates") from [Wittenberg University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wittenberg_University "Wittenberg University") in 2009,[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-Wittenberg-71)[Wheaton College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wheaton_College_(Massachusetts) "Wheaton College (Massachusetts)") in 2011[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-WheatonCollege-72) and [Butler University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Butler_University "Butler University") in 2012.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Stengel#cite_note-Naylor-73)
